Usage: mcpjam cloud projects servers [options] [command]
List and manage the servers saved in a project
Options:
--project <id-or-name> Project name or ID (defaults to the most recently
updated project)
-h, --help display help for command
Commands:
create|add [options] Create a saved MCP server
get [options] Get one saved MCP server
revisions [options] List a saved server's stored revisions, newest
first: captures of its tools and server info
revision [options] Read one stored revision of a saved server: its
tools and server info
revision-diff [options] Compare two stored revisions of a saved server:
tools added, removed and changed, and server info
changes
update [options] Update one saved MCP server
delete|remove [options] Delete one saved MCP server
connect [options] Connect an MCP server URL to a project, authorizing
in a browser if needed
connect-status [options] Check a connection request started by `server
connect`
connect-cancel [options] Cancel a pending connection request started by
`server connect`
## `cloud projects servers` commands
Manage the MCP servers saved in a project and connect new ones. All `projects servers` commands require an `sk_` API key (via `--a
pi-key` or the `MCPJAM_API_KEY` environment variable) or a prior `mcpjam cloud login`.
### Shared platform flags
| Flag | Description |
| `--api-key <key>` | MCPJam `sk_` API key (overrides `MCPJAM_API_KEY`) |
| `--api-url <url>` | MCPJam API base URL (defaults to `https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1`) |
| `--api-header <header...>` | Extra request header as `"Name: value"`, repeatable — for a deployment behind Cloudflare Access, a
WAF, or a corporate proxy. Also `MCPJAM_API_HEADERS`, one per line. Cannot set `authorization`, `idempotency-key`, or `content-typ
### `cloud projects servers connect`
Start a connection request for an MCP server URL. Discovery, browser consent, and validation happen asynchronously. When the serve
r requires OAuth, the command prints a private authorization link and (by default) opens it in a browser. The command then polls u
ntil the request reaches a terminal status.
| Flag | Required | Description |
| `--url <url>` | Yes | MCP server URL to connect |
| `--project <id-or-name>` | No | Project name or ID |
| `--server <id>` | No | Existing server ID, when the project has several on this URL |
| `--name <name>` | No | Name for the server, if one is created |
| `--reauthorize` | No | Force a fresh authorization |
| `--no-browser` | No | Print the authorization link instead of opening it |
| `--no-wait` | No | Return as soon as the request is created |
With `--no-wait`, the command prints the request id and exits immediately. The request continues in the cloud; use `connect-status
` to check it and `connect-cancel` to stop it.
